title: AI 3D generation finally hit the point where the mesh is actually usable
author: libriarian-fighter
selftext:
I make games and I’ve mostly given up on AI 3D tools — the models look great in a screenshot but import them into Unity and it’s triangle soup. Can’t animate, tanks the framerate, useless for anything that moves. Tried Dro recently (it’s an MCP inside Claude) and ran the same prompt through it and a couple of other tools to compare the wireframes — the topology difference genuinely surprised me. Clean, low-poly, dropped into URP and it just worked.  
  
Comparison below. How’s everyone else handling AI assets — actually shipping with them yet, or still just blockouts?

comments.author: Donjuante
comments.body: It really is much more optimized, but this comparison ended up being a bit poor. Ideally, it would be two fighter jets, since they're far more complex than a small single engine airplane.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: It's intentionally deceptive. Just like pretending that all the major 3D model gens out there don't have Smart TOPO already is also deceptive... especially when you realize that this is just a used car salesmen site, where they aren't providing an actual product and instead are just pointing your requests at one of the aforementioned major 3d gens and upcharging you for the privilege. Probably adding something to the prompt like, "Make it pretty more-er" at the end and think it's a valuable service.

replies.author: libriarian-fighter
replies.body:
Full disclosure — I'm involved with the project. But I also actually build games, and this exact problem (great-looking mesh, useless in engine) is why I got involved in the first place.

The value isn't pretending to have a secret foundation model — it's the pipeline: generation + automatic retopology + game-engine optimization, all inside Claude, so assets land in the same conversation where the code is written. Raw output from the big gens isn't game-ready — that's the gap. Happy to show the full unedited workflow if you're interested.

replies.author: libriarian-fighter
replies.body: Fair point, that's on me. The prompt was the same, but the outputs ended up apples-to-oranges, which makes the comparison look worse than it needed to. Running a proper one now — same object, two jets, wireframes side by side, screen-recorded start to finish. Will post the follow-up.

comments.author: isthisavirus101
comments.body: Mostly interested in a 3d tool which doesn't result in a super crappy non riggable model

replies.author: libriarian-fighter
replies.body: That's exactly the problem I'm focused on — riggable, clean-topology output instead of scan-soup. DM me if you want to try it on your own prompts, would genuinely love feedback from someone who'll actually rig the result.

replies.author: libriarian-fighter
replies.body: Honestly fair lmao. Same text prompt, but yeah — can't really compare a jet to a prop plane. Redoing it properly with identical objects, will share.
